sections.h2: Bridgeport and the offices that handle its property tax
sections.html:
Bridgeport is Connecticut's most populous city, with 148,654 residents in 2020. It sits in eastern Fairfield County where the Pequonnock River reaches Long Island Sound, about 60 miles from Manhattan. Property tax is split between two city offices: the Tax Assessor values property, and the Tax Collector bills and collects.

The city was incorporated as a town in 1821 and as a city in 1836, and it covers 19.4 square miles, 16.0 of them land. Its elevation is only 3.3 feet, a fact worth remembering when buyers raise flood and storm questions. Because Bridgeport grew as a port and factory city, its housing varies a great deal in age and condition from one neighborhood to the next.

The bill is the assessed value of the property multiplied by the mill rate. One mill is $1 of tax for each $1,000 of assessment. For fiscal year 2026-2027 the rate is 27.95 mills on real estate and personal property and 31.75 mills on motor vehicles.

Assessed value is a set share of market value, described by the city as 70 percent, so the figure on your notice will be lower than a sale price. When you check a bill, compare it with the assessed value on the notice, not with what a neighbor's house sold for. The Tax Collector's general tax information page posts the mill rate history, and the Tax Assessor's page explains how taxes are determined.

Property tax is assessed as of October 1, levied the following July 1, and paid in two installments. Connecticut law makes an installment delinquent if it is not paid by the first day of the next month.

InstallmentDueDelinquent if unpaid after
FirstJuly 1August 1
SecondJanuary 1February 1

The city files liens on June 30, the last day of the fiscal year, so ask the collector whether one has been filed against your property.

sections.h2: Interest and how payments are applied
sections.html:
Under Connecticut General Statutes section 12-146, the delinquent portion of a tax accrues interest at 18 percent a year from the date it was due. Any part of a month is counted as a whole month. The minimum charge is $2 per installment, unless the municipality has voted not to impose it, and interest keeps running even after the city wins a judgment.

The collector applies a partial payment to interest first and principal second. A payment is on time if it went through a municipal electronic payment service within the allowed time, or if the envelope carries a postmark within that time.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Bridgeport assessment
sections.html:
Appeals go to the Board of Assessment Appeals, and the written appeal must be filed on or before February 20. State law lets you file in writing or by email, in the way the board prescribes. Ask the Tax Assessor's office for the current year's application form. The appeal needs to include:

  • The owner's name, plus the signer's name and position.
  • A description of the property.
  • A name, mailing address and email address for all correspondence.
  • The reason for the appeal and your own estimate of value.
  • The signature of the owner or authorized agent, with the date.

The board must notify each filer of the hearing date, time and place no later than March 1, and the notice has to go out at least seven calendar days ahead. For commercial, industrial, utility or apartment property assessed above $1 million, the board may decline to hold a hearing, and the owner can then go directly to Superior Court under section 12-117a.

If the assessor received an extension, the filing deadline moves to March 20 and hearings take place in April. A gross assessment the board changes stays fixed until the next revaluation, with limited exceptions for new construction, damage, demolition, court orders and factual corrections.

A person who took title after the assessment date can also appeal, and so can a lessee bound by a recorded lease to pay the real property taxes.

sections.h2: Flood zone questions for a coastal house
sections.html: Bridgeport's location on the water brings storm and flood questions that inland towns face less often. Hurricanes and tropical storms hit the Connecticut coast in 1903, 1938, 1944, 1954, 1960, 1985 and, with Hurricane Sandy, in 2012. A buyer, insurer or lender may ask whether your home sits in a flood zone, and older basements, roofs and sea walls draw the most attention. Gather any flood insurance papers and repair records before you list.

sections.h2: Selling with unpaid Bridgeport property tax
sections.html:
Get a payoff figure from the Tax Collector before closing, because interest at 18 percent a year keeps adding to a delinquent balance. A closing agent can pay the tax out of the sale proceeds as long as the figure is current on the closing date.

  • List which installments are unpaid, July, January or both, and the fiscal years they belong to.
  • Ask for the interest to date and the amount that will be added each month if closing slips.
  • Check whether a lien was filed on the last June 30.
  • If you believe the assessment is wrong, the February 20 appeal date is firm, so do not wait until a closing is scheduled.

sections.h2: What a cash sale does with an unpaid bill
sections.html:
When taxes are behind, a cash sale can still close. The buyer purchases the house as is, the title company gets the payoff figure, and the amount owed is paid from the proceeds at closing. Because no lender is involved, nobody needs to be satisfied by a bank appraisal. Bring your notices, any lien paperwork and the mortgage servicer's details to the first conversation.

Expect the title company to ask three things. Which installments are open? Has a lien been filed? Is anyone besides the owner of record entitled to sign? Answering those at the start keeps a closing date from slipping, which matters because each extra month adds interest to a delinquent bill.

faqs.q: What is the Bridgeport mill rate?
faqs.a: For fiscal year 2026-2027 the city lists 27.95 mills for real estate and personal property and 31.75 mills for motor vehicles. One mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessment.

faqs.q: When are Bridgeport property taxes due?
faqs.a: In two installments, July 1 and January 1. Under state law an installment becomes delinquent if it is not paid by the first of the following month.

faqs.q: What interest does Bridgeport charge on late tax?
faqs.a: Connecticut General Statutes section 12-146 sets interest on the delinquent part at 18 percent a year, with a $2 minimum per installment unless the city votes not to impose it. Each part of a month counts as a whole month.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Bridgeport assessment?
faqs.a: The written appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals is due on or before February 20, or March 20 if the assessor was granted an extension.

faqs.q: Can a new owner appeal an assessment from before the purchase?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 12-111 lets a person to whom title was transferred since the assessment date appeal to the board.
